name: ratfor
why: Rational Fortran is a preprocessor from the 1970s that turns structured control flow into Fortran, a fine piece of computing history.

brief.what_it_is: Linux Ratfor is a command-line preprocessor that takes Ratfor source, a Fortran dialect with structured control flow (the README's own description is only that Ratfor is short for Rational FORTRAN), and emits FORTRAN 77 source. You then compile that output with a separate FORTRAN 77 compiler such as GNU Fortran. The README mentions a -s command-line option that changes the type of array elements generated for strings. The page says the program is derived from public domain ratfor 1.0 and has been maintained with bug fixes and buffer-overrun hardening.
brief.why_it_exists: The page frames Ratfor as a way to write Fortran with rational control structures, and notes it was used in the Software Tools text by Kernighan and Plauger. This Linux version keeps the public-domain tool buildable and patched; the README does not state a broader motive.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the translation mechanism in detail. It says the preprocessor outputs FORTRAN 77, which is then compiled by a standard Fortran compiler. Its change history mentions include-file handling, string directives, and data-statement ordering, which are the parts of the preprocessor it touches most.
brief.install_notes: Downloads are source tarballs ratfor-1.07.tar.gz back to 1.01, plus binary and source RPMs from the author. You need a FORTRAN 77 compiler, such as GNU Fortran from GCC, to compile and run the generated output. The 1.01 change notes say the source was adapted for GNU autoconf, so a configure-and-make build is likely, but the README gives no explicit build steps. The page gives no Homebrew-specific notes.
brief.standout: It is a preprocessor from the Software Tools era that is still being patched: the latest release, 1.07, is dated 2025-01-13, and the recent changes are security-style buffer-overrun fixes rather than new features. Its public-domain lineage is spelled out on the page.
brief.status: maintained. The change history runs from 1.01 (2001) through 1.02 (2015), 1.03 (2015), 1.04 (2020), 1.05 (2020), 1.06 (2024-12-08), to 1.07 (2025-01-13), so the author has been releasing recently. The README contains no explicit maintenance statement, and the 2001 release note says the author considered it stable.
brief.caveats: Output is FORTRAN 77, so you need a separate F77 compiler, and the README does not describe the full Ratfor syntax. The README documents a limit of 60 characters for quoted-string include filenames. The string directive needs eos defined, and the 1.05 note says it emits a warning if that is missing. The 1970s date from the Homebrew scout note does not appear in the README; the page only says Ratfor was used in Kernighan and Plauger's Software Tools. The page calls the code public domain, and says it is still in the public domain. Contact is by email to brg at dgate.org.
quotes: Ratfor is short for Rational FORTRAN.
The ratfor preprocessor outputs FORTRAN 77. Please note that you will need a FORTRAN 77 compiler (such as GNU Fortran, part of the GNU Compiler Collection) to compile and run the output of Ratfor.
I consider this program to be stable.
